thread:
mira: Quick follow-up from the instrumentation RFC — can we agree on a slimline path for edge services so we don't blow up ingest costs when we flip the pre-enrich flag?

sam: +1 we need a concrete fallback. My proposal: default lightweight trace header (trace_id, span_id, svc) + optional envelope for heavy traces behind a feature flag.

cory: Do we have metrics on current header size distribution? curious how much traffic would move between tiers.

mira: I pulled a 48h sample — median header payload ~520 bytes, p95 ~4.1kb. If we trim to the lightweight header we estimate ~40% ingest reduction for edge hosts.

jia: Sounds promising. Risk: late enrichment (customer-id, billing-key) will be harder if we drop fields at the edge. How are we carrying cost attribution?

sam: Plan: attach a cheap routing token in lightweight header that lets the gateway request a delayed enrich call. Delayed enrich would add attributes before we write to cost pipeline. That keeps tail latency unaffected.

cory: Concern: delayed enrich increases complexity and reordering. Query-side joins will need to tolerate late-arriving attributes. We already have backfill jobs but those are heavy.

mira: Agreed. Tradeoff matrix I posted in the RFC:
```
Option A: Full header (current) -> Simple joins, high ingest cost
Option B: Lightweight + delayed enrich -> Lower cost, needs late-attr handling, eventual backfill
Option C: Sampled full header -> Mix of both, sampling bias for cost metrics
```

jia: For billing we need near-100% fidelity. Sampling will break things. So either B with guaranteed enrich for billing-class traffic, or A for billing routes.

sam: Let's do B plus a deterministic routing rule: routes flagged as billing or high-value get guaranteed enrich at edge (still compact headers but run enrich sync). Everything else uses delayed enrich. That keeps billing fidelity without full ingest explosion.

cory: Implementation notes: gateway needs a per-route config flag (sync_enrich: true/false), plus an async enrich queue with idempotent enrichment and TTL. Also add an attribute version header so consumers know if attrs may arrive late.

mira: Good call on attribute version. Also we should publish a schema change window and include a middleware shim to rewrite legacy headers for 6 weeks.

jia: Ops checklist: update consumer pipelines to tolerate null billing-key for 15s and then reconcile. Add a small QPS budget for sync enrich for billing routes.

sam: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/+/3124 — includes gateway flag, async enrich queue, and test harness. Please review.

mira: Next steps: 1) Review PR by EOD Thu, 2) Run canary on staging with 10% of edge hosts using lightweight path, 3) Verify billing accuracy via synthetic traffic, 4) Ramp config. Anyone blocking?

cory: None from infra side but need acks from billing/metrics owners. I'll loop them in. :eyes:

jia: I'll run synthetic billing tests once PR is in.

ingest-bot: deploy status: enrich-queue-service -> green (deploy 2/2) :white_check_mark:

mira: Thanks all — if we can get PR reviews today we can start the staging canary on Friday. I'll send a short rollout RFC to #product and #support explaining the late-enrich behavior.

sam: One tiny nit: in the PR, reduce the default async enrich TTL from 60s -> 30s to limit reprocessing window.

mira: Done in branch. Updated tests.

cory: I'll post a short runbook for what to do if we see billing-key backlog.

mira: Great. Closing this thread once PR is merged. Thanks everyone!
